title: Flight Orchestrator: staged control-plane pivot and rollback automation for VPC deployments
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a Battle-tested 'Flight Orchestrator' that automates staged control-plane pivots for Private (VPC) deployments using Terraform/IaC, with deterministic canary cohorts, automated health gating, and safe rollback. Scope includes Terraform module extensions (tenant fractionation, traffic-siphon resources), an operator-side minimal-downtime promotion flow, preflight simulations, and post-promotion sanity checks.

Motivation: Current private control-plane upgrades are manual and error-prone. We need an automated, auditable workflow that supports: cohorted promotions (by tenant/slice), traffic siphoning for shadow validation, automatic rollback on degradation, and a repeatable Terraform-driven runbook for customers on Private Plan.

Design Highlights:
- Terraform: extend modules to support "promotion cohorts" with resource tags and a traffic-siphon target group. Add a dry-run flag to generate a plan-only promotion for preflight validation.
- Orchestration: a new Flight Orchestrator service (stateless controller) will coordinate canary waves by invoking Terraform apply plans via the CI runner and calling the Private Control Plane operator API to toggle routing.
- Health gates: multi-tiered checks: synthetic request latency P50/P95 thresholds, error-rate delta (%) vs baseline, KV-cache-hit ratio, and tail-CPU/GPU pressure. Each gate has a configurable window and tolerance.
- Rollback triggers: soft-triggers (alerts to engineers if metric drift < critical), hard-triggers (immediate rollback if error-rate > 2x baseline or latency P95 regresses > 250ms).
- Test harness: preflight simulator that replays production-like traces against the candidate control-plane in a shadow network (no production traffic). Terraform plan outputs used to validate resource diffs and potential drift.
- Auditing: every promotion run produces an immutable artifact (plan, diffs, health snapshots, operator traces) stored in S3 and indexed in the Console audit view.
- Safety features: tenant fencing (quarantine failing tenants), staged DB migration pre-conditions check, and operator-level compatibility matrix enforcement (CRD and API version checks).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Terraform modules accept "cohort_count" and "cohort_selector" inputs and produce plan-only artifacts.
2) Flight Orchestrator can run a 3-wave promotion (5% / 25% / 70%) automatically with configurable gate thresholds.
3) Automated rollback completes within a guaranteed RTO and leaves prior control-plane version healthy and reachable.
4) Runbook and CI job exist: promotion can be executed via CI pipeline with a single flag for dry-run vs apply.
5) Telemetry and plan artifacts surfaced in Console and linked to the promotion run.

Out-of-scope for initial rollout: full UI in Console (we'll provide links to promotion runs), and multi-region cross-account pivoting (follow-up PR).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should cohort sizes be by default? (security and customer SLA suggest conservative defaults.)
- Do we support DB schema migrations in the same automated flow, or require manual gating? Recommendation: require manual approval for any schema change in wave 1.
- Placement of orchestrator: run as Redwood-managed control plane job or customer-owned in their VPC? Initial plan: Redwood-managed with VPC-tunneled control-plane calls to minimize customer infra changes.
